A TEST OF THE INVALIDATION MECHANISM AGAINST FOUR REAL CASES, 2026-08-31 — direct evidence for choosing among the six options on `dec:idea-how-does-the-graph-learn-what-a-session-invalidated`, which was recorded 2026-08-23 when only two sightings existed.

═══ OPTION B WAS BUILT, AND IT WORKS ═══
That node's option B — "capture-session ASKS THE INVALIDATION QUESTION" — has shipped: capture-session carries test 7, and `unclaimed_findings` computes the candidates. Run today it behaved correctly: 2 candidates returned, `subjects_examined: 4`, and on judgement NEITHER was mine to close (one was the live output-schema control arm, one was my own fact from the same day). No false closure, no silence mistaken for an all-clear.

═══ 🛑 AND IT WOULD HAVE REACHED AT MOST ONE OF THE FOUR STALE RECORDS THIS SESSION ACTUALLY FOUND ═══
① `fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred...` — TemporalFact, subject `cap:mcp-surface`, which this session's changes DID touch. REACHABLE in principle. Found by reading it, before any computation was run.
② `dec:idea-should-optimize-be-a-served-skill-any-project-can-run` — A DECISION, asking whether to build a skill that exists and has run twice. 🛑 STRUCTURALLY OUT OF REACH: `unclaimed_findings` returns TemporalFacts only.
③ `fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to` — TemporalFact, subject `cmp:verify`. This session's changes never touched `cmp:verify`, so the subject-changed path would not have surfaced it. Found by reading `schema/verify.yaml` while checking something else.
④ `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` — A DECISION whose prose describes a flat ten while the graph holds 8 subsystems plus 2 systems of five. 🛑 OUT OF REACH for the same reason as ②.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING NONE OF THE SIX OPTIONS NAMES: HALF OF THEM WERE DECISIONS, AND THE WHOLE MECHANISM IS TEMPORALFACT-ONLY. Option A's proposed detector (`stale_measurement`) is defined over `basis: measured` TemporalFacts with no `valid_to`; options C, D and E all key on findings of that same kind. A Decision has no `valid_to` and no equivalent — its `status` moves only on the owner's word, correctly — so a Decision whose text has been overtaken by events has NO mechanism at all, proposed or built.

⇒ ALL FOUR WERE FOUND BY READING, NOT BY ANY COMPUTATION. Two by following a citation, one by opening a schema file for an unrelated reason, one by counting nodes to answer a different question.

═══ ⚠️ BOUNDS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS SERIOUS ═══
· n = ONE SESSION. Four instances in one day on one design is not a rate.
· 🛑 THE FOUR ARE NOT INDEPENDENT DISCOVERIES. Finding the first one PRIMED the search: after ①, this session was actively alert to staleness, and ②–④ were found by a reader looking for exactly that. A session not primed would plausibly have found one and carried on. That cuts BOTH ways — it inflates the count, and it means the unprimed case is worse rather than better.
· It does not measure how many stale records this design holds. The 2026-08-23 figure — 267 open facts, 200 whose subject has since changed — remains the only estimate, and it is an upper bound rather than a count.
